correctness.rationale: The Nyström rank-one eigenvalue is the exact Rayleigh quotient proved in RESULT.md. Operator monotonicity of the target matrix power makes the error positive semidefinite and identifies its nuclear norm with a trace difference. The quotient of two squared independent real Gaussian entries has the beta-prime density used in the explicit rescaled integral. The exhibited integrable majorant justifies dominated convergence for every stated real exponent and integer power-pass count; integration by parts evaluates the coefficient using a beta integral. The sharp regimes follow by comparison with the exponent boundary. The exact unit-power identity is an elementary beta-prime resolvent integral, and the coupled almost-sure claim follows from the pointwise expansion. The bundled Python checker reports CHECKS_OK algebra=100 quadrature=16 constants=2. Finite tests supplement the all-parameter proof.

Gittens–Mahoney Theorem 4 provides a trace tail bound plus a gap-suppressed squared pseudoinverse-sketch term. For a one-dimensional Gaussian leading sketch that term has infinite mean, so the estimate does not determine the present expectation.

originality.rationale: The sharp one-column transformed-trace asymptotic for every fixed positive power-pass count, in particular the two-pass expectation rate and the one-pass matrix-square-root boundary, is not supplied by either inspected defining source. The funNyström paper gives multi-column expectation bounds requiring at least two target and oversampling columns; Gittens–Mahoney gives a deterministic alignment-dependent trace bound whose leading-sketch inverse second moment is infinite for one Gaussian column. Neither dominates this finite nonlinear expected trace law. Prior unpowered rank-one residual behavior is explicitly credited. An unindexed specialized two-dimensional calculation remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A specialized unindexed two-by-two Gaussian power-Nyström derivation might contain the same coefficient.
The sharp model is two-dimensional and does not establish high-dimensional stability or comparable behavior under oversampling.
The ordinary one-pass untransformed residual law is previously understood; the claimed priority is restricted to the combined all-pass and all-matrix-power transformed-trace equivalent.

value.rationale: The defining algorithm is designed for trace and matrix-function approximation, so the smallest nontrivial sketch size is a motivated stress case. For one power pass the square-root target has a strictly positive limiting expected excess despite almost every coupled realization approaching the rank-one optimum, and larger matrix-power exponents produce diverging mean excess. One additional pass restores asymptotic mean-optimality across the stated full operator-monotone matrix-power range with a sharp rate. This natural sampling-versus-function-smoothness boundary informs what an expected-error guarantee can conceal; it is explicitly restricted to two eigenvalues.
